newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Mass. official guilty of accepting gratuities.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Mass. official guilty of accepting gratuities.

text.p: A federal jury found the former chairman of the Massachusetts House insurance committee guilty of accepting illegal gratuities late Wednesday.

Francis Woodward, who served as head of the insurance between 1985 and 1991, was found guilty of receiving more than $9,000 in free trips, golf outings, meals and tickets to events from a lobbyist representing John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Co.
Among the gratuities was an $1,800 trip to the 1986 Super Bowl in New Orleans that Woodward received from the Life Insurance Association of Massachusetts Inc, a trade association.
Each year, Woodward filed financial interest statements as required by law, but he failed to disclose any of the payments from the insurance lobbists.
The case marked the first time that a lawmaker's state gratuity-disclosure forms, which are filed under penalty of perjury, had been used in a criminal prosecution.
Woodward was convicted on five counts of conspiracy, wire and mail fraud, and violating the Travel Act. He faces up to five years in prison and $250,000 in fines on each of the counts.
